title: Filter pushdown: a raising filter crosses a join, and runs on one input even when the other is empty
verdict: raising filters kept above projections; pushed into join inputs, outside the reference's loose model only when the other input is empty (probed: it raises)
description: Undocumented. In the optimizer at v2.0.0, a filter that can raise (`CanThrow`) is not pushed through a projection: it stays on top (`pushdown_projection.cpp`), and filter pullup keeps fallible predicates below a projection. Only internal barrier expressions (`__internal_barrier`, for secure views) are held above every operator that can remove rows (`FilterPushdown::Rewrite`).

An inner join is turned into a cross product whose conditions and the filters above it are pushed to the side they reference, with no `CanThrow` test (`pushdown_inner_join.cpp`, `pushdown_cross_product.cpp`); a left join pushes its left-side filters the same way (`pushdown_left_join.cpp`), and the join order optimizer moves filters to the lowest join that binds them. A filter over a filter merges both conjunct lists, the upper one first.

The reference's issue analysis already allows most of this: filter and join conditions are evaluated on `Rel.loose`, the input with filters removed and inner joins widened to cross joins (`analysis/Sverify/Analysis/Safety.lean`), so a `WHERE` over an inner or left join covers every row of each input, and a merged filter covers the rows the lower filter would remove. The gap left is an empty other input: the loose cross product is then empty and the reference reports no issue, while DuckDB evaluates the pushed filter on every row of the side it was pushed into. So `SELECT … FROM a JOIN b ON a.k = b.k WHERE 10 // a.x > 1` with `b` empty appears to raise on `a.x = 0`. This is from reading the code: a probe must confirm it (the hash join may skip the probe side when the build side is empty).

The other way round, DuckDB can raise less than the reference: a `LIMIT` stops the scan, so `WHERE s::INT = 10 LIMIT 1` does not raise on the unconvertible rows after the first match (DuckDB's test). That keeps the no-error guarantee.

Round 3 (engine tests): test_barrier.test pins it: with `join_filter_pushdown` off, `SELECT … FROM secrets JOIN allowed ON … WHERE s::INT = 42` raises on the secret row the join removes, and `__internal_barrier` keeps the filter above the join. A `LIMIT` above a raising scan filter stops the scan before the bad rows (test_throwing_filter_pushdown.test).

Round 4 (probes): with `b` empty, `SELECT * FROM a JOIN b ON a.k = b.k WHERE 10 // a.x > 1` raises `Division by zero` on `a`'s row with `x = 0`; so do the cast `a.s::INTEGER > 1` and `b LEFT JOIN a` with the filter on `a` (the filter makes the join inner). `EXPLAIN` shows the filter in `a`'s scan. With `b = {2}`, the row `k = 1, x = 0` is removed by the dynamic join filter in the scan before the division runs, and nothing raises; with `join_filter_pushdown` disabled it raises, on a row the reference's loose model also evaluates. So the empty other input is the case outside the reference.
No upstream test pins a raising filter pushed below a join whose other input is empty; it may change between versions.
reference: The reference evaluates an expression only on the rows its operator sees: a `CASE` branch on the rows that reach it, a filter's condition on the rows below it, a join condition on the pairs it forms. Its issue analysis (`Rel.HasIssue`, `analysis/Sverify/Analysis/Safety.lean`; docs/how-it-works.md) trusts the engine's evaluation order: `CASE` is lazy, `AND`/`OR` are not, and filter and join conditions may run before the filters below them. A plan `verify` reports error-free must run without error, so an engine that evaluates a raising expression on rows outside that model breaks the guarantee. sverify's DuckDB SQL writes a filter over a join as a `WHERE` over the join, which the optimizer is then free to push.

provenance.notes: Confirms round 1's reading: inner joins (via the cross product) and the left side of left joins push filters into their inputs whatever CanThrow says; only projections, filter pullup through projections, full-outer coalesce pushdown and derived bounds test it. Filter over filter merges both conjunct lists, upper first, so a raising upper conjunct can run before the lower filter's guard. Checked against the reference's loose model (Rel.loose, analysis/Sverify/Analysis/Safety.lean L1031-L1075): filter conditions are evaluated on the input with filters removed and inner joins widened to cross joins, so a WHERE over an inner or left join already covers every row of each input, except when the other input is empty (the cross product is then empty while DuckDB still scans the pushed side). The description's 'which the reference never evaluates' overstates the gap; see the round 2 report.

evidence.note: Rel.loose: filters removed, inner joins as cross joins; HasIssue evaluates filter and join conditions on it
